{{Quote|But the ritual was not confined to the doomed Sith Lords. They were but the eye of the storm; the center of a vortex that spread across the entire planet. Every man, woman, and child on Nathema died that day. Every beast, bird, and fish; all the insects and plants; every living being touched by the Force was consumed. When the ritual ended, Nathema was no longer a world. It was a husk sucked dry. Lord Vitiate sacrificed millions, stealing their life force to make himself immortal. Their deaths also made him stronger than any Sith who had come before, and he ceased to be known as Lord Vitiate. On that day, the Emperor was truly born.|[[Darth Nyriss]]|<ref name="Revan" />}}
During the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] developed a '''ritual''' of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]] that granted him [[Immortality/Legends|immortality]] and immense strength in the Force by ensaring the souls of the dead. Using the strength of eight thousand [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Lords to power the Sith magic, Vitiate was able to [[Ritual of Nathema|strip]] [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] itself from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Nathema]] at the expense of every living thing on the world, and as the Sith Emperor of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]], he later developed an artificial version of the ritual by combining it with [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] and [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]]. With the Sith magic, the Emperor was able to grant immortality to his favored servants, and he intended to use the ritual on a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] scale in order to consume all life in the galaxy and thereby ensure that he would never be defeated. However, the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] known as the [[Hero of Tython]] prevented the Emperor's agents from bringing about the sacrifice of thousands of lives that was necessary to start the ritual&mdash;but only for a time. With his plans exposed to the Empire, a now dethroned Vitiate turned on the Imperial world [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] and used the strength of the entire world's population to [[Ziost crisis|carry out the ritual once more and consume all life on Ziost]].

==Description==
{{Quote|He dominated their minds, crushed their resistance. He turned them into slaves to his will, forcing them to participate in the most complex ritual of Sith sorcery ever attempted. Calling on the dark side, Lord Vitiate devoured them. He fed on their power, absorbing it into himself, utterly obliterating all traces of his victims.|Darth Nyriss|<ref name="Revan" />}}
[[File:Tenebrae_of_Nathema.jpg|thumb|250px|left|Tenebrae of Nathema, the creator of the ritual]]
The ritual developed by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] was a complex piece of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]] that required an immense amount of strength and power in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] to complete.<ref name="Revan" /> It required a sacrifice&mdash;death on a massive scale&mdash;to begin, and the ritual allowed the user to devour [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] essence of the dead, empowering themselves at the cost of their victims' lives.<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance" /> Upon the ritual's completion, the Sith magic expanded across the target world as a wave of energy<ref name="The End of It All">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=general|The End of It All|Ziost}}</ref> and literally stripped [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] from the targeted [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Revan" /> in less than a [[Standard minute/Legends|minute]],<ref name="The End of It All" /> [[Death/Legends|killing]] all remaining living beings instantly and transferring their life force and power into the ritual's user.<ref name="Revan" />

When he [[Ritual of Nathema|first orchestrated]] the rite on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Nathema]],<ref name="Revan" /> Vitiate drew upon the strength of eight thousand other Sith Lords to power his Sith magic,<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref > and it took ten [[Standard day/Legends|days]] to complete in its entirety.<ref name="Revan" /> [[Standard century/Legends|Centuries]] later, Vitiate&mdash;now as the Sith Emperor&mdash; was able to accomplish the ritual on the planet [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] using only his own immense strength in the Force.<ref name="The End of It All" /> On Nathema, Vitiate used the ancient [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] known as [[Zildrog]] to achieve the necessary death toll,<ref name="Zildrog">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=codex|Zildrog}}</ref> and on Ziost, he [[Possession/Legends|possessed]] the cosmopolitan planet's population and set them upon each other.<ref name="The End of It All" />

[[File:Fleeing_death.png|thumb|right|220px|Citizens of Ziost are turned to ash as they flee the expanding wave of Sith magic.]]
Living matter, whether it was the bodies of people or plants, was turned to ash at the moment it was touched by the Sith magic, though some prone bodies retained their shape like ash sculptures of the ritual's victims. The trunks of trees were left standing as solid ash, and the Sith magic even destroyed a number of stone statues on Ziost. Only a handful of creatures were capable of surviving the ritual besides Vitiate&mdash;[[Sithspawn/Legends|Sithspawn]] known as [[Monolith]]s,<ref name="The End of It All" /> which had been created from dark side energy rather than by mutating a living creature like typical Sithspawn.<ref name="Monolith">{{TORcite|type=codex|Monolith}}</ref> The act also destroyed almost all technology on the planet, overloading the circuits of [[Droid/Legends|droids]] and wiping out their [[Memory bank/Legends|memory cores]]. The rite leeched [[Color/Legends|color]], sound, and heat from reality itself, leaving the targeted planet a brown, barren, and lifeless world upon which the absence of the Force could cause anything alive on its surface&mdash;especially [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]]&mdash;to die if they stayed there long enough.<ref name="Revan" />

The Emperor later developed an artificial form of the ritual by merging it with [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] and [[Cybernetics/Legends|biomechanical enhancements]], forgoing the need for a sacrifice. The artificial process involved the insertion of dozens of wires and IV tubes into the subject's body, which connected the individual to a series of generators and vats filled with bubbling green liquid. As the subject opened themselves to the dark side, the Emperor and his machines stripped away their mortality over the course of a few [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]], leaving the recipient in constant pain for the rest of their existence.<ref name="Revan" /> Both the original and artificial versions of the Sith magic left the subjects unable to appreciate their physical senses to the degree that others did,<ref name="Eternal Emptiness">{{TORcite|type=conversation|Lord Scourge|Eternal Emptiness}}</ref> as they sacrificed their ability to feel emotions in return for [[Immortality/Legends|immortality]].<ref name="Revan" />

==Applications==
{{Quote|The darkness will consume all it touches. Stars will burn black, ashes raining on lifeless worlds. Everything ends.|The [[Force ghost/Legends|ghost]] of Meetra Surik|<ref name="TOR:TJP">{{TORcite|type=faction|Republic|The Jedi Prisoner|the ''Telos''}}</ref>}}
[[File:Surface_of_Nathema.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The surface of Nathema after the ritual]]
As a result of the ritual of Sith magic, Vitiate became immortal and gained immense strength in the Force.<ref name="Revan" /> After [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] of further study into the dark side, the Sith Emperor developed the strength to repeat the ritual on his own, and he intended to magnify its effects on a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] scale. If successful, the ritual would have allowed him to consume the life of every living thing in the galaxy, and the Emperor would have absorbed it to become like a [[Deity/Legends|god]].<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance" /> The Emperor utilized the artificial ritual to grant immortality to a few select servants, including the twelve [[Servant]]s of the secretive organization known as the [[Hand of the Empire|Emperor's Hand]]. Another who received immortality through the ritual was the Sith Lord [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]], who was appointed the [[Emperor's Wrath]]&mdash;the Sith ruler's personal enforcer&mdash;for his loyalty.<ref name="Revan" />

==Users==
{{Quote|A thousand years ago, the Emperor tricked an entire Sith world into aiding a dark ritual. He promised great power. Only for himself, of course. The ritual consumed every living thing on the planet. He absorbed those life essences through the Force.|Lord Scourge|<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance" />}}
The only known user of the immortality rite was the Sith Emperor, a Sith Lord originally known as Vitiate.<ref name="Revan" /> In [[4999 BBY]],<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire's]] defeat in the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Vitiate summoned the remaining Sith Lords of the Empire to his homeworld of Nathema. There, he [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|dominated the minds]] of the eight thousand Sith who answered his call and forced them to participate in the Sith magic,<ref name="Revan" /> and turned the Zildrog superweapon against his subjects.<ref name="Zildrog" /> The resultant death toll, filtered through the ritual,<ref name="Boyd">{{TORweb|url=community/showthread.php?p=9593256|text=Charles Boyd on Forums: "Was Vitiate a fraud then? Confused about a line from the FP (spoilers obviously)"}}</ref> conferred immense power and immortality upon himself at the expense of every living thing on the world.<ref name="Revan" />

The newly-empowered Sith Emperor blamed the effects of the event<ref name="Revan" />&mdash;known to history as the Ritual of Nathema&mdash;<ref name="History 30">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 30: Rise of the Sith Emperor}}</ref> on the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who had destroyed the Empire in the Great Hyperspace War, and he gathered the survivors of the Empire before leading them on a [[Sith exodus|twenty-year exodus]] from the [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Worlds]].<ref name="Revan" /> Not long after he [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted the Empire]] on the world [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] in [[4980 BBY]], the Emperor gathered twelve [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith purebloods]] and performed the artificial version of the rite upon them, granting them immortality and appointing them as the Servants of the Emperor's Hand, though during the ritual he bound their life forces to his own so that he could draw on their strength to sustain him.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

In [[3950 BBY]], almost a thousand years later, the Emperor decided to reward the Sith Lord Scourge with immortality after he betrayed the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Meetra Surik]] by killing Surik during the Jedi's [[Attack on the Sith Emperor|attempt]] to slay the Emperor. The Emperor performed the artificial rite in the depths of the [[Imperial Citadel (Sith Empire)|Imperial Citadel]] on Dromund Kaas, and made it clear to his new Wrath that the pain caused by the ritual would never pass.<ref name="Revan" /> As a result of Revan and Surik's attack,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> the Emperor became determined to ensure his survival at the expense of the entire galaxy, and he made the necessary preparations for repeating the ritual on a galactic scale. Three centuries later, during the [[Galactic War]] between the Republic and his Empire, the Emperor ordered his agents to cause the necessary sacrifice of thousands of deaths,<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance" /> though their efforts were foiled by the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] known as the [[Hero of Tython]].<ref name="Doomsday">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Doomsday|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>

[[File:Ziost_dying.png|thumb|right|250px|A view of Ziost from space, as the ritual expands across the planet.]]
The Sith Emperor was grievously wounded in [[Dromund Kaas operation|battle]] with the Hero, and was forced into hibernation on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] until a now-mad Revan tried to restore the Emperor to strength in order to permanently destroy the Emperor. Revan's plans failed, but the Emperor fed off of the deaths caused by [[Battle of Yavin 4 (Galactic War)|battle]] against [[Order of Revan|Revan's followers]], thus restoring his strength. Disowned by the Empire he once ruled, Vitiate&mdash;now a Force entity without a body&mdash;began exerting influence over the population of the planet [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]]. His reach soon extended across the world, allowing him to possess virtually the entire population and set them against each other in a frenzy of death.<ref name="The End of It All" />

Despite attempts by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the Empire to break Vitiate's control over Ziost, he continued to consolidate his strength and created monstrous Sithspawn known as Monoliths. Using Sith magic as he did on Nathema, Vitiate fed off the dead and unleashed a wave of energy across the globe, turning all living beings to ash and warping reality&mdash;Ziost's tundra became a gray wasteland where colors seemed muted.<ref name="The End of It All" /> [[1000 BBY/Legends|Thousands of years]] later, the Sith Lord [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] discovered a transcription about the ritual and its effects within the [[Darth Revan's Sith Holocron|Sith Holocron]] of Revan, and used it to develop the technique known as the [[thought bomb]].<ref name="Force">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Sith Emperor's ritual was first introduced in [[Drew Karpyshyn]]'s [[2011]] novel ''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]'',<ref name="Revan" /> and it is a major plot point in Act III of the Jedi Knight class storyline in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''.<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance" /> The storyline for the planet Ziost introduced in Game Update 3.2 concludes with Vitiate using the ritual to consume all life on Ziost, and represents the first visual depiction of the ritual and its aftermath.<ref name="The End of It All" /> Game Update 5.9: "The Nathema Conspiracy" [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the origins of the Ritual of Nathema, adding the involvement of the Zildrog superweapon,<ref name="Zildrog" /> although the game's head writer, [[Charles Boyd]], clarified that Zildrog was used to instigate the death toll necessary for the ritual, just as the Emperor's agents attempted in the Jedi Knight storyline.<ref name="Boyd" />
